title: From Student to Work Visa: What the Change Involves
summary: A status change is a fresh application, not a renewal. The window has a hard end, the fee rose sharply on 1 October 2026, and there is no appeal.
body_html:
Getting a job offer is the easy half. Converting Student status into a work status is a separate application, judged separately, and it has a shape worth knowing before you are standing in it.

It is a fresh application under Article 20 [source:1]

A change of status is for a foreign national who is changing the purpose of their residence and will carry out activities falling under a different status. [source:1] The procedural basis is Article 20 of the Immigration Act. [source:1]

The application window runs from when the grounds for the change arise until the expiry date of your current period of stay. [source:1]

That end point is hard, and it is the thing to plan against. Your window is not "when my job starts" — it is your existing period of stay. If your status expires in March and your job starts in April, the application happens inside the March boundary.

The warning attached to the window

The agency adds a note at exactly this point in its own page: if you are not carrying out the activities of your current status, your status may be cancelled. [source:1]

This matters because of what the gap between graduation and employment looks like in practice. You finish your course. You are no longer studying. Your status still says Student. The agency has written down that not carrying out your status's activity is a cancellation risk.

So the period after your course ends is not neutral waiting time. It is the period your application needs to already be in.

The fee changed on 1 October 2026, and not by a little [source:1]

This is new enough that most advice you will find has the old figure.

The counter-application fee now depends on the period of stay you are granted. [source:1] Up to 3 months is 10,000 yen. [source:1] Over 3 and up to 6 months is 18,000 yen. [source:1] Over 6 months and under 1 year is 25,000 yen. [source:1] 1 year is 33,000 yen. [source:1] Over 1 and under 3 years is 48,000 yen. [source:1] 3 to under 5 years is 64,000 yen. [source:1] 5 years or more is 75,000 yen. [source:1]

The agency states that applications received by 30 September 2026 are charged the pre-revision fee of 6,000 yen, even where permission comes on or after 1 October. [source:1]

Read those two paragraphs together and the scale is clear: a change granted with a 1 year period went from 6,000 yen to 33,000 yen. [source:1]

Where certain requirements are met the fee may be reduced or waived, and the reduced fee is 10,000 yen regardless of the period granted. [source:1] The fee for online applications is set separately. [source:1] Counter payment is by revenue stamp, so buy it before you go. [source:1]

One consequence nobody mentions: because the fee scales with the period granted, a longer period costs more up front and less per year. The length you are granted is now a financial matter, not just a convenience.

How long it takes, and what the published figures show

The standard processing period is 1 month to 2 months. [source:1] There is no appeal procedure. [source:1]

The agency also publishes actual average processing days by status. In the most recently published month, a status change to Engineer / Specialist in Humanities / International Services — the status most language school graduates move into — averaged 72.9 days. [source:2]

Set that against the standard period of up to 2 months. [source:1] The published average sits above it, and the figure excludes rejections and withdrawn applications, so it describes cases that were granted. [source:2]

That is the number to plan with, not the standard period. And it is why the window matters: an application filed close to your expiry date is an application whose processing time you cannot afford.

What is actually being judged

The same guideline governs changes and renewals, and the considerations are the same. [source:3] Two of them bite harder on a change than on a renewal.

Conformity with the landing permission criteria is required in principle at a change, not only at entry. [source:3] For a work status, those criteria are where the relationship between your education and the job sits — which is the real reason a change gets refused, far more often than anything about conduct.

And having carried out your current status's activity is a consideration. [source:3] A student who stopped attending is bringing that into the application.

The quieter items apply too: tax and National Health Insurance arrears, treated as negative factors where serious; and the notification obligations. [source:3] Those are cheap to get right and awkward to explain away.

What to do, in order

  • Work backwards from your expiry date, not your start date. [source:1] The window closes at expiry.
  • File early. The published average for this change was 72.9 days in the latest month published. [source:2] The standard period says up to 2 months. [source:1] Treat the longer number as real.
  • Do not drift after your course ends. Not carrying out your status's activity is a cancellation risk, and the agency says so on the application page itself. [source:1]
  • Budget the fee properly. It depends on the period granted and rose on 1 October 2026. [source:1] Check whether you qualify for the reduction. [source:1]
  • Clear any tax or insurance arrears first. [source:3] This is the cheapest thing on the list and the most often skipped.
  • Keep your attendance clean to the end of the course. It is a consideration in an application you have not filed yet. [source:3]

For the full set of considerations, including the fee change as it applies to ordinary renewals, see what immigration actually looks at when you renew. If your course is ending and you are unsure about the gap, what happens if you stop attending or withdraw covers the cancellation side. For the notifications you owe regardless, see what you must report and by when.

Fees, processing figures and the guideline are all revised, and the processing averages are published monthly. The agency's pages linked below are the authority. This page is a summary and not legal advice; applications are decided case by case and, as the agency states, satisfying every consideration is not sufficient on its own.

claims_without_sources: 学歴と職務内容の関連性について、どの程度の一致が求められるか —— 上陸許可基準の中身は省令の管轄で、本記事の出典からは確認していない。「そこが争点になる」と述べるに留め、基準の内容は書いていない。
不許可率・許可率 —— 公表されていない。処理期間の公表値も不許可・取下げを除外しているため、率は算出できない。
就職活動のための「特定活動」への変更（卒業後の継続就職活動）—— 別の在留資格・別の告示の管轄で、本記事の出典では扱っていない。卒業後の空白期間については取消しのリスクに触れるに留めた。
オンライン申請の手数料額 —— 申請ページは別ページを案内するだけで額を示していない。「別に定められている」とだけ書いた。
減額・免除の要件 —— 「一定の要件を満たす者」とあるのみ。減額後の額（10,000円）は出典に明記があるため書いた。
72.9 日という平均が「技術・人文知識・国際業務」の行のものである対応 —— PDF の表には多数の在留資格の行があり、闸门は数字の存在しか検証できない。表をパースして行の対応を突き合わせた（書き手の責任として確認）。
